concepts.label: babysitter process
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the monitor process that restarts the cluster manager on crash; not previously named as a concept anywhere else in the corpus, only surfaced here via this hidden command's --vm option

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-server-eshell
relations.evidence: The couchdb vm runs the views service on each data node and the ns\_server vm corresponds to the cluster manager. By default the vm option is set to ns\_server.

relations.subject: server:cluster-manager
relations.evidence: The babysitter vm is a monitor that ensures the cluster manager is always running and is restarted in the event of a crash or error.

notable_absence.finding: This is the single most dangerous command in the entire batch by its own admission - 'This is a hidden command and is not intended for typical production use... improper use can lead to the cluster being placed in an unusable state' - yet it states no RBAC role or permission requirement whatsoever, only a prose warning to 'Check with the Couchbase Support team before running this command.' Every other page in this batch that touches a comparably consequential operation (node-reset.md) at least names a role informally; this page, guarding direct unsupported access to the cluster manager's internals, names none at all.

cross_component_finding: This page is the only place in the corpus that names the babysitter process and describes the three-VM internal architecture (babysitter / couchdb / ns_server) of a running Couchbase Server node - genuinely new, substantive architectural vocabulary, surfaced only because this hidden debugging command happens to expose it as a --vm enum. It is also terser and more literal than the equivalent explanations found on concept pages elsewhere in the corpus: the couchdb vm is dismissed in one clause ('runs the views service on each data node') with no cross-reference to the already-deprecated Views engine concept, and no page anywhere else in the corpus mentions 'babysitter' at all - a piece of real product architecture that exists in exactly one, lightly-reviewed, explicitly-unsupported reference page.
cross_product_finding: Plainly none - this command connects to a local Erlang process on a self-managed Server node; it has no meaning in Capella's managed deployment model, and the page states as much implicitly by restricting itself to 'localhost' only.
